growth_signal.value: Raised a $140M round in 2026 backed by Anthropic, Nvidia and Menlo Ventures, more than double its $60M round from 2024.

raised.value: $140M Series C (2026), after a $60M round in 2024

entry.idea: Designing new medicines usually relies on the same small set of lab-known genes, so Basecamp Research collects genetic material from remote places like rainforests, oceans and hot springs and uses it to train AI models that help design new medicines.
entry.lesson: When everyone is competing over the same public datasets, go collect a rare dataset nobody else has and turn it into a lasting advantage.
entry.name: Basecamp Research

growth.basis: substitute: funding round bigger than the last, with new marquee investors (Anthropic, Nvidia)
growth.reason: Went from a $60M round in 2024 to a $140M round in 2026 with major new backers, though no user or revenue numbers are public.

market.reason: AI-driven drug discovery and genetic medicine is a huge, fast-growing global market for pharma and biotech.

tech.reason: Its dataset of genetic material from remote, rarely-sampled ecosystems is very hard for competitors to gather or copy quickly.

entry.twist: Instead of training its AI mostly on data other labs already have, it built its own huge, unique database of genetic diversity gathered from extreme and rarely-sampled environments around the world.
entry.who_pays: Pharmaceutical and biotech companies, plus investors, who want better AI tools for discovering and designing new drugs and genetic medicines.
entry.why_now: AI models are only as good as their training data, and interest in AI-designed medicines and biology is at an all-time high, making a rare, large genetic dataset very valuable.
